strengths: The idea of using a VLM's Yes/No log-odds as a fully differentiable semantic and spatial critic is clean and well-motivated, and the paper convincingly demonstrates its versatility by plugging the same reward into two very different paradigms (SDS-style optimization and test-time guidance of a native 3D DiT sampler).

Quantitative results on the GPTEval3D benchmark (Table 1) show consistent improvement over all baselines across all six metrics, including strong reward-model baselines like DreamReward and DreamDPO, which supports the central claim for the optimization-based paradigm.

Ablations in Sec. 5.3 are informative: removing the geometric query or switching to single-view input both degrade quality (Janus artifacts, floating parts), directly supporting the dual-query and multi-view design choices.

The limitations section is honest and specific, acknowledging that the reward under-utilizes the VLM's visual reasoning on long prompts and identifying concrete future directions (disentangled semantic/geometry feedback, hierarchical query engineering).
weaknesses: The evaluation of the feed-forward/test-time-guidance paradigm is weak and potentially cherry-picked. Table 2 is computed only 'on all cases shown in Fig. 1 and 4' — a handful of hand-selected failure cases — rather than a broad prompt set or standard benchmark. The sweeping claim that test-time guidance 'actively steers the iterative sampling process of SOTA native 3D models to correct severe spatial errors' is thus not supported by statistically meaningful evidence.

There is a metric inconsistency in Table 2: CLIP-D is marked with a downward arrow (implying lower is better) and VLM3D's 0.19 is bolded as best, yet the text claims 'the substantial gain in CLIP-D demonstrates that our rVLM effectively steers the sampling process towards better text-semantic alignment.' Either the arrow or the interpretation is wrong; this kind of error undermines confidence in the quantitative analysis.

Potential evaluation circularity: the method optimizes toward a VLM's judgment, and the primary benchmark evaluation (GPTEval3D) is itself performed by a VLM judge (GPT-4o-mini). While the judge differs from the reward backbone, VLM-judged metrics plausibly favor outputs shaped by VLM feedback; no human study is provided to confirm the gains transfer to human preference.

Novelty is modest relative to the framing. Backpropagating through VLM/CLIP logits as a differentiable reward is well established in 2D generation and reward-model literature, and prior works already use VLM-style rewards in text-to-3D (e.g., DreamReward/DreamDPO). The 'dual-query' design is essentially two criteria concatenated into a single prompt with a single log-odds signal; no ablation compares this against separate semantic/geometry rewards, which weakens the claim that the dual-query formulation is a core contribution.

Key methodological details needed for reproducibility are missing or deferred: the number of rendered views N, view selection, how the gradient ∇_{z_t} r_VLM in Eq. (10) is obtained through the differentiable rendering of an intermediate DiT latent prediction, memory/compute overhead of backpropagating through a 7B VLM at every sampling step, and the annealing schedule for λ_VLM are all unspecified in the main paper (and no supplementary material is included with the submission).

The test-time guidance is only compared against the unguided baselines (CLAY, Hunyuan3D); there is no comparison with alternative refinement or test-time-guidance strategies for feed-forward 3D models, so the relative merit of the approach within this paradigm is unknown.

Writing and bibliography are sloppy in places: duplicate references ([1]/[3] and [28]/[29], [43]/[44]), a typo ('guidace'), and inconsistent notation, which suggests the manuscript needed another careful revision pass.

The premise that VLMs provide reliable 3D spatial understanding is asserted but not validated in isolation (e.g., how well does the Qwen2.5-VL critic's Yes/No judgment correlate with actual geometric defects?), so gradient noise and reward-hacking behavior of the critic are not characterized.
